question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & 4 \\ -3 & 2 & -6 \\ -2 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -13 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{33}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & 4 \\ -3 & 2 & -6 \\ -2 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 2 & -6 \\ -2 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -13 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3}.$
